title: Evaluating Classifiers
body:
Suppose we trained a logistic regression classifier for some binary classification task. The true labels $$y$$ and predicted probabilities $$P(Y=1|x)$$ are given below, one bullet per observation:
• true label $$1$$, predicted probability $$0.9$$
• true label $$1$$, predicted probability $$0.6$$
• true label $$0$$, predicted probability $$0.6$$
• true label $$0$$, predicted probability $$0.55$$
• true label $$1$$, predicted probability $$0.4$$
• true label $$0$$, predicted probability $$0.3$$
In order to make predictions, we need to threshold $$P(Y=1|x).$$ We use our thresholds as follows: the prediction $$\hat{Y}$$ is $$1$$ when $$P(Y=1|x)\geq{T}$$ and $$0$$ when $$P(Y=1|x)<T$$
We want to decide between three possible thresholds for $$P(Y=1|x)$$
• Model A uses a threshold of $$T=0.25$$
• Model B uses a threshold of $$T=0.5$$
• Model C uses a threshold of $$T=0.75$$
